profile.reading: This H5 Data Centers facility is located at 200B Meadowlands Parkway, Secaucus, New Jersey 07094, in Hudson County. The building totals more than 38,000 square feet, built to a Tier III design with 2N UPS power, multiple diesel generators with 48 hour runtime, and N+1 cooling. The page states SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS compliance and 10 on net carriers with 100 Gbps options. No MW capacity figure is published for this specific building. A January 31, 2022 H5 Data Centers press release documents that this Secaucus, New Jersey facility was one of seven data centers, alongside sites in Nashville, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Portland, St. Louis, and St. Paul, Minnesota, that H5 acquired from vXchnge in a deal totaling more than 250,000 square feet of data center space and over 150 customers, expanding H5's portfolio to 20 markets at the time. The St. Paul, Minnesota facility acquired in that same deal is this registry's separate H5 Minneapolis row. H5 Data Centers is a privately held US colocation and wholesale data center operator with facilities spanning roughly two dozen markets nationwide, per the company's own site. This Secaucus building sits in the Hudson County data center corridor across the Hudson River from Manhattan, a market anchored by major carrier hotels and colocation campuses including Equinix's own Secaucus facilities and Evocative's EWR1 building already on file elsewhere in this registry. H5 is not a publicly traded company and does not file SEC disclosures, so this entry's specifications are sourced to the operator's own published facility page and its own acquisition press release rather than an independently audited source, a limitation this registry notes rather than treats as disqualifying, consistent with its general practice for privately held colocation operators. No MW capacity figure or year opened date was located for this specific building.

reading.body:
H5 Secaucus occupies more than 38,000 square feet in the Hudson County data center corridor across the Hudson River from Manhattan, a market anchored by major carrier hotels and colocation campuses. The facility is built to Tier III design with 2N UPS power, multiple diesel generators with 48 hour runtime, and N+1 cooling. No megawatt capacity figure is published for this building, so its size relative to other AI compute hubs cannot be determined from operator disclosures.

The building holds SOC 2 Type II certification, indicating it qualifies to process data subject to audit and control attestation requirements. It holds ISO 27001 certification, indicating information security management system design. It holds PCI-DSS certification, indicating it qualifies to process payment card data. Ten on-net carriers with 100 Gbps options are available, a specification common to colocation facilities serving financial services and enterprise tenants rather than hyperscale AI operators.

H5 acquired this facility from vXchnge in January 2022 as one of seven regional data centers totaling more than 250,000 square feet across Nashville, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Portland, St. Louis, St. Paul, and Secaucus. New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities and publishes megawatt figures for five of them, totaling 111.3 MW. This campus does not appear in that published total, ranking it outside the state's disclosed capacity baseline and making its relevance to AI scaling unquantifiable from available operator data.
